title: Finite-free change of completed coefficients preserves integral constructible complexes
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, let $E\subset E'$ be finite extensions of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation rings $A=\mathcal O_E\subset B=\mathcal O_{E'}$ and uniformizers $t=\varpi_E$, $v=\varpi_{E'}$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and let $T$ be a noetherian finite-dimensional scheme on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], with its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Put $R_T=\varprojlim_n(A/t^n)_T$ and $S_T=\varprojlim_m(B/v^m)_T$, the completed coefficient sheaves of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], with the canonical ring map $R_T\to S_T$ induced by $A\subset B$. Let $\Dbc(T_{\Proet},A)\subset D(\operatorname{Mod}(R_T))$ and $\Dbc(T_{\Proet},B)\subset D(\operatorname{Mod}(S_T))$ be the full subcategories of [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete] (derived completeness, uniformly bounded constructible reduction towers with common local models, and compatible etale-origin witnesses), and let $C(K)=K\otimes^L_{R_T}S_T$ be derived change of rings [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings].

Then $C$ carries $\Dbc(T_{\Proet},A)$ into $\Dbc(T_{\Proet},B)$. More precisely, let $(T_k)$ be a finite stratification of $T$ [def-constructible-stratification] such that, on each stratum $T_k$ and pro-etale locally on it, $K$ is isomorphic to $R\otimes^L_AP$ for a bounded complex $P$ of finite projective $A$-modules (here $R$ is the completed sheaf of $A$ on that stratum). Then on the same strata and the same pro-etale localizations $C(K)$ is isomorphic to $S\otimes^L_B(B\otimes_AP)$, where $B\otimes_AP$ is a bounded complex of finite projective $B$-modules with the same amplitude as $P$; the isomorphism is the image under $C$ of the given one, composed with the balancing $(R\otimes_AP)\otimes_RS\cong S\otimes_B(B\otimes_AP)$.

source.place: Exactness of T_{E'/E} (first display); the membership argument of the reviewed base proof step 1, through the stratified perfect characterization (ii) <=> (i). Agent lemma.

proof.text: Apply (i) => (ii) of [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization] to the given K over A. Its scheme hypotheses are precisely those on T, and its condition (i) includes the compatible etale-origin witnesses of the category in this item. Obtain a finite stratification and pro-etale covering members with models $R\otimes_A^L P$, where P is bounded with finite projective terms. For the more precise assertion start instead with the specified stratification, covering members and model isomorphisms; the remaining steps use exactly these choices.

source.place: Proposition 6.6.11; use the existing DAG characterization including its uniform-tower and compatible-witness clauses.

proof.text: Choose integers a <= b outside which P is zero. For each nonzero degree q, finite generators give a surjection $A^{N_q}\to P^q$. Projectivity lifts $1_{P^q}$ through this surjection, giving $i_q:P^q\to A^{N_q}$ and $p_q:A^{N_q}\to P^q$ with $p_qi_q=1$. Tensor these two maps with B: $(1\otimes p_q)(1\otimes i_q)=1$ on $B\otimes_A P^q$. Thus $B\otimes_A P^q$ is a direct summand of $B^{N_q}$, generated by the images of its standard basis and projective by the direct-summand characterization. With differential $1\otimes d_P$, these terms form a bounded finite-projective B-complex in the same interval [a,b]. Zero degrees use N_q=0. This is the asserted preservation of the chosen complex amplitude.

source.place: Tag 05CF, lemma-characterize-projective; elementary finite-generator splitting and tensoring of the splitting equations.

proof.text: On each chosen covering member, sheafify the coefficient splitting maps of step 2 as in [def-weil-pbc-strict-perfect-coefficient-package]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-strict-perfect-ringed-pullback-model] to extension from the constant A-sheaf to the completed coefficient sheaf R (the identity underlying topos). It identifies $R\otimes_A^L P$ with the termwise complex $F=R\otimes_A P$ and supplies its strict-perfect package and K-flatness. Apply the same theorem over B to the bounded complex $B\otimes_A P$: its derived realization is the termwise complex $S\otimes_B(B\otimes_A P)$. These applications use bounded finite-projective terms, not projectivity of sheaf objects in the global abelian category.

source.place: Tag 08H3, lemma-strictly-perfect-pullback; K-flat representative refinement of the existing strict-perfect ringed-pullback node.

proof.text: Let u be the restriction to a chosen stratum followed by restriction to its chosen pro-etale covering member. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-stratum-completion-unit-restriction] separately to A and B: the restricted coefficient sheaves are R and S on that member and these module restrictions are exact. The two induced scalar maps agree: their composites with every finite B-quotient are induced by the same valuation-ring inclusion, hence their maps into the limit S agree. Apply [lem-sfb-kflat-scalar-comparison-normalization] to the stratum inverse image and to the slice-topos inverse image. It gives the canonical isomorphism $u^*(K\otimes_{R_T}^L S_T)\cong (u^*K)\otimes_R^L S$. For the slice, the coefficient sheaves are their ordinary restrictions; exact slice restriction is the one in [def-weil-pbc-ringed-site-derived-restriction]. Thus both applications meet the hypothesis that source coefficients are identified inverse images; composing these comparisons gives restriction to the same covering member.

source.place: Tag 03EL, lemma-tensor-product-pullback, with K-flat normalization from the cited scalar-comparison theorem; completed restriction is the cited Bhatt-Scholze Lemma 6.5.8 consequence.

proof.text: Write $e:u^*K\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_RF$ for the specified local model, with the representative comparison of step 3. Apply local derived scalar extension to e. Since F is bounded strict-perfect, [lem-weil-pbc-strict-perfect-ringed-pullback-model] for the identity topos with structural map R -> S gives the canonical representative isomorphism $C(Q_RF)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_S(F\otimes_R S)$. Together with step 4 this identifies the restriction of C(K) with $(R\otimes_A P)\otimes_R S$. The comparison is the image of e followed by the canonical K-flat representative comparison; it therefore uses the given local isomorphism, rather than a new choice of local model.

source.place: Tag 08H3, lemma-strictly-perfect-pullback, with its specified derived-model and naturality refinement.

proof.text:
The remaining ordinary balancing isomorphism is given degreewise by
$((r\otimes p)\otimes s)\longmapsto c(r)s\otimes(1\otimes p)$,
from $(R\otimes_A P)\otimes_R S$ to $S\otimes_B(B\otimes_A P)$, where c:R -> S is the coefficient map. Its inverse sends $s\otimes(b\otimes p)$ to $(1\otimes p)\otimes sb$. The A-balancing relations agree because the two maps from A into S agree; the R- and B-balancing relations respectively move c(r) and b into the S factor. The two composites are the identity by these same relations. These balanced maps commute with restriction and with $d_P$, so their sheafifications are inverse chain maps, using the sheafified-tensor definition [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Step 3 identifies the target with $S\otimes_B^L(B\otimes_A P)$, which proves the precise local formula, on the same strata and covering members.

source.place: Sheafified balanced tensor; explicit elementary associativity/change-of-rings calculation.

proof.text: By step 2 each $B\otimes_A P$ is a perfect B-complex. Steps 4--6 give exactly condition (ii) of [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization] over B for C(K), on the finite stratification selected in step 1. Apply its implication (ii) => (i), with the original noetherian finite-dimensional T and the same invertible prime ell. The conclusion is membership in the full three-clause B-category: intrinsic derived completeness, a uniformly bounded constructible reduction tower, and compatible etale-origin witnesses. No independent assertion that arbitrary tensor commutes with inverse limits, and no identification with a constant-coefficient derived category, is needed.

Preconditions: the item is unsplit on live and side-live, it is not on the 10-19 drop list, it has no repair note, and its only citer is the reviewed parent prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension. The statement is unchanged from the base. The 4 added stmt_deps are all used. proof_deps equals the union of the uses, and there is no cycle. Steps: S1 is (i)⇒(ii) of the integral stratified-perfect characterization; its hypotheses (T noetherian, finite-dimensional, ℓ invertible) are exactly the item's. S2 is elementary: finite generators plus the projective lifting clause give a splitting, tensoring with B keeps it, and the amplitude is unchanged since B is free over A. S3 applies the strict-perfect ringed pullback model along the identity topos with ring map \underline A→R; it gives K-flatness, the package and ε_F, and the same over B. S4: stratum-completion restriction gives u^{-1}R_T≅R and u^{-1}S_T≅S, the ring maps agree after every finite projection, and the kflat scalar comparison applies because A_X=h^{-1}A_Y. That comparison is a declared generic off-unit tool use (sk-prop-scalar-six), accepted as the ND parent reviewer did. S5 applies C to the given model and composes with ε_F. S6 is explicit balancing; I checked the inverse maps and the balancing relations. S7 is (ii)⇒(i) over B with v and the same T, which gives the full three-clause category.
